Coordinated resumable cryptographic-erasure panic wipe now implemented + repo-tested on BOTH platforms (Phase F). PanicWipe is a persisted state machine (IDLE->REQUESTED->KEY_ERASED->ARTIFACTS_DELETED->NEW_IDENTITY->IDLE) with a durable WipeJournal written AFTER each idempotent step, so a crash-then-resume re-runs at most the one interrupted step. Crypto-erasure FIRST: eraseKeys() destroys the KEK before any file is deleted -- AndroidKeystore master key (_androidx_security_master_key_) on Android (invalidates every EncryptedSharedPreferences ciphertext for identity + store key), MeshIdentity.deleteFromKeychain() (both Keychain items) on iOS -- so prior data is unrecoverable once KEY_ERASED is persisted regardless of later cleanup. deleteArtifacts reuses SqliteMessageStore.panicWipe + Identity.panicWipe on Android; on iOS it now calls SqliteMessageStore.panicWipe(at:) (Phase G store hook wired). regenerateIdentity builds a fresh identity. Pure state machine + injected glue => host-testable: PanicWipeTest (Android, 7 tests) + PanicWipeTests (iOS, 7 tests via swift test + xcodebuild simulator) prove no-crash ordering (eraseKeys before deleteArtifacts before regenerate), crash-before-any-step resumes to completion with the journal at the last COMPLETED step, no destroying step double-run or skipped, resumeIfPending no-op when idle. :mesh:testDebugUnitTest 80 PASS; ios swift test 82 PASS + xcodebuild 69 PASS. NOT closed: wipe is non-shipping (:mesh / test-only GodstoneMesh, not on LIGHT path); actual Keystore/Keychain deletion + shipping-path integration are on-device.
